objective_breakdown: Three-metric task for extreme-cold NMC811/graphite battery: (1) lowT_retention >= 0.95 at -20C — primary differentiator requiring electrolyte optimization; (2) energy_density_wh_kg >= 327.18 — achievable via electrode thickness/porosity tuning; (3) energy_density_wh_l >= 880 — coupled with (2) through porosity reduction. Key trade-off: thick electrodes raise ED but worsen low-T transport; electrolyte reformulation (higher sigma at -20C) is the primary lever to break this trade-off.
candidate_strategy: R1: baseline characterization (Chen2020 1C + lowT + calc-energy). R2-4: architecture variants (thick electrode, low porosity, thin CC/separator). R5-7: electrolyte formulation (reduce EC fraction, add low-viscosity co-solvent DMC/EA for sigma improvement at -20C). R8-9: combined best-arch + best-electrolyte verification. R10: safety (4C_charge_45C).
budget_allocation: Baseline 1 round, architecture 3 rounds, electrolyte 3 rounds, combined 2 rounds, safety 1 round = ~10 rounds total
risk_and_fallback: Risk1: Chen2020 ED ceiling below 327.18 — fallback to thicker electrodes. Risk2: low-T retention vs ED trade-off — fallback to electrolyte optimization (Stage 3 electrolyte freedom). Risk3: three-strike on same cause — question system/boundary/metric assumptions.

detail: Baseline Chen2020: ED=400.29 Wh/kg (>=327.18 PASS), VED=843.49 Wh/L (<880 FAIL, gap 36.5), lowT_retention=0.9943 (>=0.95 PASS). Architecture tuning needed for VED.
ceiling_assessment: ED ceiling 400.29 well above target. VED ceiling 843.49 is 4.1% below 880. Gap achievable via porosity reduction and thinner CC. Low-T retention robust at baseline. No material escalation needed.

candidates.name: Architecture A - Low Porosity + Thin CC
candidates.role: Reduce electrode and separator porosity + thinner current collectors to compress non-active volume

candidates.name: Architecture B - Thick Electrodes
candidates.role: Increase electrode thickness by 20% for higher areal capacity and VED

candidates.name: Architecture C - Combined Aggressive
candidates.role: Aggressive VED push: low porosity + thicker electrodes + thinner CC and separator

llm_reason: VED gap is 36.5 Wh/L (843 vs 880). Three architectural approaches: (A) porosity reduction is most direct volume shrinkage lever; (B) thicker electrodes increase active material loading per area; (C) combined approach for maximum VED. Trade-off: lower porosity may reduce rate capability but 1C is moderate. Thicker electrodes increase diffusion path but ED benefit is primary.

candidates.name: Architecture C (retest safety)
candidates.role: Verify4C safety of best R2 candidate

llm_reason: Variant C passed all performance metrics (ED=418.11, VED=896.15, lowT=99.42%). Running4C safety check.

note: Performance metrics pass but4C safety FAIL: T_max=335.37K (>333.15), plating at anode_min=-0.449V. Low porosity (neg 0.20) causes transport bottleneck at 4C.

candidates.name: Architecture D - Balanced
candidates.role: Restore negative porosity to baseline 0.25 for4C transport, keep positive low porosity and thin CC for VED

candidates.name: Architecture E - Thick Pos Low Por
candidates.role: Even thicker positive electrode (90um) with low porosity for maximum VED, baseline neg porosity for transport

llm_reason: R3 showed neg_porosity 0.20 causes plating at 4C. Restored neg_porosity to 0.25 (baseline). Testing whether baseline neg porosity avoids plating while still achieving VED target through pos_porosity reduction + thick electrodes + thin CC.

note: All performance pass.4C safety FAIL: T_max=333.89K (barely over 333.15), plating anode_min=-0.427V. Thick electrodes cause4C transport issues regardless of porosity.

candidate: Architecture E - Thick Pos Low Por
note: Performance pass.4C safety FAIL: T_max=334.18K, plating. Same4C plating pattern as D and C.

candidates.name: Architecture F - Thin CC/sep
candidates.role: Moderate geometry: thin CC and separator only (no porosity change from baseline). VED improvement from thinner non-active layers.

llm_reason: R3-R4 showed that thick electrodes and low positive porosity cause plating at 4C. Variant F keeps baseline porosity (neg 0.25, pos 0.335) and only reduces CC/separator thickness. This is the minimum-risk geometry change.

note: Performance metrics ALL PASS (ED=435.12, VED=881.14, lowT=99.49%). T_max=332.65K PASS. Only plating fails (anode_min=-0.430V). BASELINE CHECK: Chen2020 baseline also plates at 4C (anode_min=-0.438V). Plating is a system-level characteristic, not caused by geometry changes.

candidates.name: F-med electrolyte
candidates.role: 50% higher electrolyte conductivity and diffusivity to improve 4C transport and prevent plating

candidates.name: F-high electrolyte
candidates.role: 100% higher electrolyte conductivity and diffusivity for maximum transport improvement

candidates.name: F-elec-part (med elec + small particles)
candidates.role: Combined electrolyte improvement + smaller particles to reduce solid-phase diffusion limitation

llm_reason: Plating is inherent to Chen2020 at 4C (verified: baseline also plates). Electrolyte reformulation + smaller particles are the remaining levers. Three variants: med electrolyte, high electrolyte, combined with small particles.

note: ED=437.93 PASS, VED=886.84 PASS, lowT=99.50% PASS, T_max=330.19 PASS. Plating persists (anode_min=-0.424V). Electrolyte improvement lowered T_max by 2.5K but insufficient to eliminate plating. BASELINE LIMITATION: Chen2020 system plates at 4C inherently.

ED=439.31 PASS, VED=889.62 PASS, lowT=99.51% PASS, T_max=331.08 PASS. Plating persists (anode_min=-0.417V). Doubling electrolyte transport not sufficient to prevent plating at 4C. Solid-phase diffusion is the rate-limiting step.

T_max=328.60K PASS (best thermal). Anode_min=-0.433V still plates. Smaller particles (3.5um vs 5.86um) + electrolyte improvement insufficient. The Chen2020 baseline plating at 4C is a fundamental system limitation requiring different electrode chemistry (e.g. SiOx blend with higher diffusivity).

endorsement.reason: real_compute=false per task default; no DFT/MD endorsement. Best design: Architecture F + medium electrolyte reformulation (sigma=1.42 S/m, D=2.65e-10 m2/s, t+=0.38).

electrolyte.rationale: Low-temperature optimized electrolyte: reduced EC fraction, increased DMC/LMC for lower viscosity at -20C

known_limitations: Lithium plating at 4C charge (anode_min=-0.424V): baseline Chen2020 system characteristic, not eliminable by electrolyte/geometry alone
Volumetric energy density 886.84 Wh/L barely exceeds 880 threshold - sensitive to manufacturing tolerances

recommendation: Architecture F + medium electrolyte reformulation achieves all three primary objectives: ED=437.93 Wh/kg (target 327.18, +33.9%), VED=886.84 Wh/L (target 880, +0.8%), lowT retention=99.50% (target 95%, +4.7%). The4C safety criterion (no plating) is not achievable with the Chen2020 NMC811/graphite system at 4C charge rate - this is a verified system-level baseline limitation (the unmodified Chen2020 baseline also plates at 4C, anode_min=-0.438V). Electrolyte reformulation improved T_max from 332.65K to 330.19K but could not eliminate plating. To achieve no plating at4C, a different electrode system (e.g. NMC811/SiOx-graphite blend with higher solid-phase diffusivity) or a fundamentally different electrolyte (e.g. ionic liquid or solid-state) would be required.

plating_4C.root_cause: Chen2020 baseline system plates at 4C inherently (verified baseline anode_min=-0.438V). This is a system-level limitation, not a design flaw.

design_iterations: 7 variants tested across 6 rounds (baseline, A/B/C architecture, D/E balanced, F thin CC, F-med/high electrolyte, F-elec-part)
